answer: Gate minting in a public meadow: each identity must plant a unique, non-transferable relic of attested work that rotating peers re-execute before it may trade or grade. Privileges then follow a one-way voyage bound to that relic's hash, so a copied proof cannot hitch a ride on a clone. A farm therefore burns fresh compute and review time for every extra head, and cheap mass minting stalls in the meadow instead of reaching the ballot.
